**\* Administrative changes.**

**\* Configuration changes.**

**\* Automation failures.**



**Logs will not contain passwords, access tokens, or unnecessary sensitive information.**



**### 13.21 Backend Security Boundary**



**The backend is a trusted application layer but must treat client input as untrusted.**



**The backend will independently enforce:**



**\* Authentication.**

**\* Authorization.**

**\* Input validation.**

**\* Resource access.**

**\* Test restrictions.**

**\* Administrative permissions.**



**The frontend will never be considered sufficient for enforcing security controls.**



**### 13.22 Backend-to-Service Communication**



**The backend may communicate with:**



**\* Supabase / PostgreSQL.**

**\* Traffic-processing services.**

**\* ML inference services.**

**\* Quantum research services where required.**

**\* Automation services.**



**Service credentials will be stored securely outside source code.**



**### 13.23 API Versioning**



**The API will be designed so that future changes can be introduced without unnecessarily breaking existing frontend functionality.**



**A versioned API structure may be used, for example:**



**```text**

**/api/v1/**

**```**



**The final versioning strategy will be selected during implementation.**



**### 13.24 Backend Goal**



**The backend will provide a secure and maintainable central layer connecting:**



**```text**

**Frontend**

&#x20;  **↓**

**FastAPI Backend**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Authentication**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Testing**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Traffic Analysis**

&#x20;  **↓**

**ML Detection**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Database**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Automation**

**```**



**The backend will therefore act as the primary control point between the user interface and the security-analysis components.**



**````**

**Step 35 — Section 14: Database \& Data Storage Architecture**



**This section defines what we store, where we store it, and what we deliberately do NOT store.**







**## 14. Database and Data Storage Architecture**



**Extension AI Guard will use a structured data-storage architecture to maintain application information, testing metadata, detection results, model information, and other required records.**



**The planned application database is PostgreSQL through Supabase.**



**Raw network captures and large generated artifacts will be handled separately from the primary application database.**



**### 14.1 Database Responsibilities**



**The application database will store information required for the platform to operate.**



**Potential database information includes:**



**- User records.**

**- Role information.**

**- User onboarding status.**

**- Extension-test definitions.**

**- Test-session metadata.**

**- Detection results.**

**- Detection history.**

**- Model metadata.**

**- ML experiment metadata.**

**- Quantum experiment metadata.**

**- Alert configuration.**

**- Audit information where required.**



**### 14.2 User Data**



**The user-related data model may contain:**



**- User identifier.**

**- Authentication-provider identifier.**

**- Display information required by the application.**

**- Assigned role.**

**- Onboarding status.**

**- Account creation information.**

**- Account status.**



**Authentication credentials will be handled by the selected authentication system rather than stored as plain application data.**



**Passwords will never be stored in plaintext.**



**### 14.3 Role Data**



**The system will maintain role information for authorization.**



**The initial roles are:**



**- Beginner.**

**- Security Analyst.**

**- Research User.**

**- Administrator.**



**Role information will be used by backend authorization logic to determine which operations a user may perform.**



**### 14.4 Extension Definitions**



**The database may maintain metadata describing the controlled extensions available in the testing laboratory.**



**Potential fields include:**



**- Extension identifier.**

**- Extension name.**

**- Description.**

**- Test category.**

**- Version.**

**- Availability status.**

**- Expected behavior category.**



**The database will not be used to execute arbitrary extension code.**



**### 14.5 Test Sessions**



**Each controlled analysis will have a test-session record.**



**Potential information includes:**



**- Test identifier.**

**- User identifier.**

**- Extension identifier.**

**- Test type.**

**- Start time.**

**- End time.**

**- Test status.**

**- Capture identifier where applicable.**

**- Processing status.**

**- Detection status.**



**A simplified test lifecycle is:**



**```text**

**Created**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Preparing**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Running**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Capturing**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Processing**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Analyzing**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Completed**



**Failure or cancellation states may also be supported.**



**14.6 Detection Results**



**The database will store application-level detection results.**



**A detection record may contain:**



**Detection identifier.**

**Test identifier.**

**User identifier where appropriate.**

**Classification.**

**Risk level.**

**Confidence or probability information where available.**

**Model identifier.**

**Model version.**

**Detection timestamp.**

**Analysis status.**

**Relevant summarized feature information.**



**The stored result will allow the frontend to display previous analyses.**



**14.7 Detection History**



**Detection history will be associated with the appropriate user and test session.**



**Users will only be able to retrieve records they are authorized to access.**



**Administrators may have broader access according to the final authorization policy.**



**The system will avoid exposing raw sensitive traffic information in ordinary history views.**



**14.8 Model Metadata**



**The database may store metadata about trained ML models.**



**Potential fields include:**



**Model identifier.**

**Model name.**

**Model version.**

**Model type.**

**Dataset version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Training date.**

**Evaluation metrics.**

**Model status.**



**The actual model artifact may be stored separately from the database depending on size and deployment requirements.**



**14.9 ML Experiment Records**



**ML experiments may be recorded with information such as:**



**Experiment identifier.**

**Dataset version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Algorithm.**

**Training configuration.**

**Evaluation metrics.**

**Experiment timestamp.**

**Selected-model status.**



**This allows the project to explain how the final model was selected.**



**14.10 Quantum Experiment Records**



**Quantum ML experiments may contain:**



**Experiment identifier.**

**Dataset version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Quantum algorithm.**

**Number of qubits.**

**Encoding method.**

**Circuit configuration.**

**Optimizer.**

**Evaluation metrics.**

**Simulator information.**

**Experiment timestamp.**



**These records will support the project's classical-versus-quantum research comparison.**



**14.11 Alert Configuration**



**The application may store alert configuration metadata.**



**Potential information includes:**



**Alert identifier.**

**User or administrator association.**

**Alert type.**

**Enabled/disabled status.**

**Trigger condition.**

**Notification destination configuration reference.**



**Sensitive credentials required for external integrations will not be stored as ordinary plaintext database values.**



**14.12 Audit Information**



**Where required, the database may store security-relevant audit records.**



**Potential events include:**



**Authentication-related events.**

**Authorization failures.**

**Test execution.**

**Administrative actions.**

**Configuration changes.**

**Detection events.**



**Audit records will avoid storing passwords, access tokens, or unnecessary sensitive content.**



**14.13 Raw PCAP Storage**



**Raw PCAP files will be treated separately from normal relational application records.**



**PCAP data may contain sensitive network information.**



**Therefore:**



**PCAP files will be stored only for controlled project testing.**

**Access will be restricted.**

**Retention rules will be defined during implementation.**

**Unnecessary captures will be removed according to the project's retention policy.**

**PCAP files will not automatically be committed to GitHub.**



**The final storage mechanism may use controlled local storage, object storage, or another appropriate deployment mechanism.**



**14.14 Processed Traffic Data**



**Processed traffic information may be stored separately from raw PCAP files.**



**The processing pipeline may generate structured records such as:**



**Flow identifiers.**

**Packet counts.**

**Byte counts.**

**Duration.**

**Timing statistics.**

**Protocol information.**

**Feature values.**



**Only the information required for the analysis and research workflow will be retained.**



**14.15 Dataset Storage**



**ML datasets will be maintained separately from normal application records.**



**The project will distinguish between:**



**Raw Traffic**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Processed Traffic**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Feature Dataset**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Training Dataset**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Evaluation Dataset**



**Dataset versions will be tracked so that model results can be associated with the dataset used to train and evaluate the model.**



**14.16 Data Versioning**



**Important datasets and model-related resources will use version identifiers.**



**For example:**



**Dataset: v1**

**Features: v1**

**Model: RF-v1**

**Model: XGB-v1**

**Quantum Experiment: QML-v1**



**The exact versioning format will be finalized during implementation.**



**14.17 Data Access Control**



**Database access will follow the principle of least privilege.**



**The system will enforce appropriate controls so that:**



**Users cannot access other users' private records.**

**Beginner users cannot access administrative information.**

**Analysts cannot automatically modify model configurations.**

**Research users cannot automatically perform administrative operations.**

**Administrators receive only the privileges required for their responsibilities.**



**Backend authorization will remain the primary application-level enforcement mechanism.**



**14.18 Data Protection**



**Sensitive application data will be protected through appropriate security controls.**



**The project will use:**



**HTTPS for data transmitted between deployed services.**

**Secure authentication.**

**Role-based authorization.**

**Environment-based secret configuration.**

**Restricted database access.**

**Controlled access to PCAP files.**

**Appropriate retention policies.**

**14.19 Data Minimization**



**The system will follow a data-minimization approach.**



**The project will avoid collecting or storing information that is not required for:**



**Testing.**

**Detection.**

**Evaluation.**

**Research.**

**Auditing.**

**Application functionality.**



**Controlled and synthetic information will be preferred during testing whenever practical.**



**14.20 Database Backup and Recovery**



**The deployment environment will define appropriate backup and recovery procedures for important application data.**



**The recovery strategy will consider:**



**Database backups.**

**Configuration recovery.**

**Model artifact recovery.**

**Dataset recovery where required.**



**Backup credentials and sensitive backup information will be protected.**



**14.21 Database Goal**



**The database architecture will provide reliable storage for the application's structured information while keeping large, sensitive, or generated artifacts appropriately separated.**



**The overall storage architecture is:**



**Supabase / PostgreSQL**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Application Records**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Users**

**Tests**

**Detections**

**Models**

**Experiments**

**Audit Data**



**Separate Storage**

&#x20;       **↓**

**PCAP**

**Datasets**

**Model Artifacts**

**Generated Reports**



**This separation improves maintainability, security, scalability, and deployment flexibility.**



**Section 15: Extension Laboratory Architecture**



**This is one of the core parts of Extension AI Guard.**



**It defines how our two controlled extensions, test server, browser environment, traffic capture, and analysis pipeline work together.**





**## 15. Extension Laboratory Architecture**



**The Extension Laboratory is the controlled testing environment of Extension AI Guard.**



**Its purpose is to generate reproducible browser-extension network behavior so that the traffic-analysis and detection pipeline can identify differences between normal and suspicious activity.**



**The laboratory will be isolated from ordinary user browsing and will use controlled project infrastructure.**



**### 15.1 Laboratory Components**



**The Extension Laboratory will contain the following major components:**



**- Browser testing environment.**

**- Benign Extension.**

**- Suspicious Traffic Simulator.**

**- Controlled Test Server.**

**- Data Sink.**

**- Network Traffic Capture.**

**- PCAP Processing Pipeline.**

**- Feature Extraction Pipeline.**

**- ML Detection Engine.**



**The overall architecture is:**



**```text**

**Browser Testing Environment**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;  **Controlled Extension**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;  **Controlled Test Server**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;    **Network Traffic**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;  **TShark / Wireshark**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;       **PCAP**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;**Packet \& Flow Processing**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;   **Feature Extraction**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;    **ML Detection**

&#x20;         **↓**

&#x20;   **Security Result**

**15.2 Browser Testing Environment**



**The browser environment will be dedicated to controlled project testing.**



**The environment will be used to install and execute the project extensions for experimental purposes.**



**The testing environment should not be treated as the user's normal personal browsing environment.**



**Testing will use controlled configurations so that experiments can be reproduced.**



**15.3 Benign Extension**



**The Benign Extension will provide a normal behavioral baseline.**



**Its purpose is to generate legitimate browser-extension network activity that can be used as a baseline for comparison.**



**The extension may perform controlled operations such as:**



**Requesting project-controlled resources.**

**Performing normal periodic requests.**

**Sending predefined harmless test data.**

**Communicating with the controlled test server.**



**The extension will use only the permissions required for its intended test behavior.**



**15.4 Suspicious Traffic Simulator**



**The Suspicious Traffic Simulator will generate predefined suspicious-looking network behavior inside the controlled laboratory.**



**Its purpose is to provide labeled examples for detection development and demonstrations.**



**The simulator will use controlled project infrastructure and synthetic test information.**



**Possible experimental behaviors may include:**



**Unusual request frequency.**

**Repeated communication patterns.**

**Abnormal request sizes.**

**Unusual timing patterns.**

**Suspicious destination characteristics within the controlled environment.**

**Background communication patterns.**

**Encoded or high-entropy test payload characteristics.**



**The simulator will not be designed to attack arbitrary third-party systems.**



**15.5 Controlled Test Server**



**The Controlled Test Server will provide the destination infrastructure used by the project extensions.**



**Its responsibilities include:**



**Receiving controlled test requests.**

**Recording request metadata.**

**Providing predictable responses.**

**Supporting repeatable experiments.**

**Acting as a controlled data sink.**



**The server will be reachable only according to the laboratory configuration.**



**15.6 Data Sink**



**The Data Sink will receive synthetic test information generated by the controlled extensions.**



**The data sink allows the system to observe and record test behavior without requiring real sensitive user information.**



**Test data should therefore be:**



**Synthetic.**

**Non-sensitive.**

**Reproducible.**

**Clearly associated with the laboratory.**

**15.7 Extension Permissions**



**Extension permissions will follow the principle of least privilege.**



**Only permissions required for the defined experiment will be requested.**



**The project will avoid unnecessarily broad permissions.**



**Permission requirements will be documented so that users and reviewers can understand why each permission exists.**



**15.8 Extension Configuration**



**The extensions will use controlled configuration values.**



**Configuration may identify:**



**Test-server endpoint.**

**Test mode.**

**Experiment identifier.**

**Test duration.**

**Test behavior profile.**



**Sensitive credentials will not be hard-coded into the extension source code.**



**15.9 Test Profiles**



**The laboratory may support predefined test profiles.**



**Example:**



**Profile 1**

**Normal Baseline**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Benign Extension**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Expected Normal Traffic**



**Profile 2**

**Suspicious Behavior**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Suspicious Traffic Simulator**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Controlled Suspicious Traffic**



**Profile 3**

**Custom Research Test**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Selected Experimental Configuration**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Traffic Analysis**



**The exact profiles will be implemented after the laboratory foundation is completed.**



**15.10 Test Lifecycle**



**Each laboratory test will follow a controlled lifecycle:**



**Test Created**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Environment Checked**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Extension Selected**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Test Server Prepared**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Traffic Capture Started**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Extension Test Started**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Traffic Generated**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Capture Stopped**

&#x20;     **↓**

**PCAP Stored**

&#x20;     **↓**

**PCAP Processed**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Features Extracted**

&#x20;     **↓**

**ML Analysis**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Result Generated**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Test Completed**



**If an error occurs, the test will enter an appropriate failure state.**



**15.11 Traffic Capture**



**Network traffic generated during the laboratory experiment will be captured using project-approved tools such as:**



**TShark.**

**Wireshark.**



**The capture system will record the traffic required for analysis.**



**Capture configuration will be controlled by the test workflow.**



**15.12 PCAP Handling**



**PCAP files will be treated as sensitive analysis artifacts.**



**The system will:**



**Generate captures only during controlled tests.**

**Associate captures with test identifiers.**

**Restrict access to authorized users.**

**Avoid committing captures to GitHub.**

**Apply retention rules.**

**Remove unnecessary captures when appropriate.**

**15.13 Packet Processing**



**After capture, the processing pipeline will convert raw network traffic into structured information.**



**The processing flow is:**



**Raw PCAP**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Packet Parsing**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Flow Identification**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Flow Aggregation**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Statistical Extraction**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Feature Dataset**



**The processing system will validate input files before analysis.**



**15.14 Flow Analysis**



**The system will group related packets into network flows where applicable.**



**Potential flow information includes:**



**Source information.**

**Destination information.**

**Protocol.**

**Source and destination ports.**

**Packet count.**

**Byte count.**

**Flow duration.**

**Packet timing.**

**Directionality.**



**The exact feature set will be finalized during the ML feature-engineering phase.**



**15.15 Controlled HTTPS Testing**



**Where encrypted traffic is required for experiments, the laboratory will use project-controlled infrastructure.**



**The project may use a controlled TLS termination point so that traffic behavior can be studied safely within the laboratory.**



**The architecture will not attempt to bypass encryption on arbitrary third-party systems.**



**15.16 Reproducibility**



**Laboratory experiments should be reproducible.**



**Each experiment will attempt to record:**



**Extension version.**

**Test profile.**

**Test-server configuration.**

**Capture configuration.**

**Dataset version.**

**Feature version.**

**Model version.**

**Experiment timestamp.**



**This allows detection results to be traced back to the conditions under which they were generated.**



**15.17 Beginner Testing Experience**



**A beginner user will not need to manually configure the complete laboratory.**



**The Guided Testing Mode will perform the required workflow through the application.**



**The user experience will be:**



**Choose "Start Guided Test"**

&#x20;         **↓**

**AI Assistant Explains Test**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Choose Benign or Suspicious Test**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Start Test**

&#x20;         **↓**

**System Performs Controlled Capture**

&#x20;         **↓**

**System Analyzes Traffic**

&#x20;         **↓**

**User Receives Security Result**



**The user will receive explanations at each important stage.**



**15.18 Expert Testing Experience**



**Experienced users will be able to access deeper information.**



**The expert workflow may expose:**



**Test Configuration**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Capture Configuration**

&#x20;     **↓**

**PCAP**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Flow Information**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Feature Values**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Model Prediction**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Detection Evidence**



**This allows analysts to investigate why a particular result was produced.**



**15.19 Laboratory Safety Controls**



**The Extension Laboratory will operate under controlled conditions.**



**Safety controls include:**



**Controlled destinations.**

**Synthetic test data.**

**Restricted extension permissions.**

**Isolated testing environment.**

**No uncontrolled third-party targeting.**

**No unnecessary collection of personal information.**

**Restricted access to captured traffic.**

**Test execution authorization.**

**15.20 Laboratory Separation**



**The laboratory will remain logically separated from the main production application.**



**The architecture is:**



**Production Application**

&#x20;       **│**

&#x20;       **│ Controlled API**

&#x20;       **▼**

**Testing Orchestration**

&#x20;       **│**

&#x20;       **▼**

**Extension Laboratory**

&#x20;       **│**

&#x20;       **▼**

**Controlled Test Infrastructure**



**The production application will not directly execute arbitrary browser-extension code.**



**15.21 Laboratory-to-ML Boundary**



**The laboratory will produce traffic data.**



**The ML system will consume validated processed features rather than arbitrary executable content.**



**The boundary is:**



**Extension Laboratory**

&#x20;       **↓**

**PCAP**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Validated Processing**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Feature Dataset**

&#x20;       **↓**

**ML Inference**

**15.22 Laboratory Goal**



**The primary goal of the Extension Laboratory is to create a safe, repeatable, measurable environment for studying browser-extension network behavior.**



**It provides the foundation for:**



**Traffic capture.**

**Dataset creation.**

**ML training.**

**ML evaluation.**

**Detection demonstrations.**

**Beginner education.**

**Classical versus quantum experiments.**

**Security research.**



**Section 16: Traffic Capture \& Packet Processing Architecture**



**## 16. Traffic Capture and Packet Processing Architecture**



**The Traffic Capture and Packet Processing subsystem is responsible for collecting network traffic generated inside the controlled Extension Laboratory and converting the captured traffic into structured information that can be used by the machine-learning detection pipeline.**



**The subsystem will separate raw packet capture, packet parsing, flow processing, feature extraction, and ML inference so that each stage can be independently tested and validated.**



**### 16.1 Traffic Analysis Pipeline**



**The complete traffic-analysis flow is:**



**```text**

**Controlled Browser Extension**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Network Traffic**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Traffic Capture**

&#x20;         **↓**

**PCAP File**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Packet Parsing**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Flow Reconstruction**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Traffic Statistics**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Validated Feature Set**

&#x20;         **↓**

**ML Detection Engine**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Security Result**

**16.2 Traffic Capture Tools**



**The initial traffic-capture tools will include:**



**TShark.**

**Wireshark.**



**TShark will be suitable for automated capture and command-line processing.**



**Wireshark will be used primarily for manual inspection, debugging, validation, and demonstration.**



**The exact capture configuration will be determined during implementation.**



**16.3 Capture Lifecycle**



**A controlled capture will follow this lifecycle:**



**Prepare Test**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Validate Environment**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Start Capture**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Start Extension Test**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Generate Controlled Traffic**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Complete Test**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Stop Capture**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Validate PCAP**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Store Capture Metadata**



**The system will associate the resulting capture with the corresponding test session.**



**16.4 Capture Configuration**



**The capture subsystem may configure:**



**Network interface.**

**Capture duration.**

**Capture filters.**

**Output location.**

**Test identifier.**

**Maximum capture size where appropriate.**



**Capture parameters will be controlled by the testing workflow rather than allowing unrestricted user-defined capture behavior.**



**16.5 PCAP Validation**



**Before processing, the system will validate the captured file.**



**Validation may include:**



**File existence.**

**File format.**

**File readability.**

**File size.**

**Capture completion status.**

**Associated test identifier.**



**Invalid or incomplete captures will be marked appropriately rather than silently processed.**



**16.6 PCAP Storage**



**Raw PCAP files will be treated as sensitive analysis artifacts.**



**The storage workflow is:**



**PCAP Generated**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Validation**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Controlled Storage**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Processing**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Retention / Deletion Policy**



**Raw captures will not automatically be committed to GitHub.**



**16.7 Packet Parsing**



**The packet-processing layer will read validated PCAP files and extract packet-level information.**



**Potential packet information includes:**



**Timestamp.**

**Source address.**

**Destination address.**

**Source port.**

**Destination port.**

**Protocol.**

**Packet length.**

**Direction.**

**Transport information.**



**Only information required by the analysis pipeline will be retained.**



**16.8 Flow Reconstruction**



**Individual packets will be grouped into logical flows where appropriate.**



**A flow may be represented using information such as:**



**Source**

**Destination**

**Protocol**

**Source Port**

**Destination Port**

**Start Time**

**End Time**



**The system will use a consistent flow-identification strategy throughout dataset generation and inference.**



**16.9 Flow Statistics**



**The processing pipeline will calculate statistical properties for each flow.**



**Potential statistics include:**



**Total packet count.**

**Total byte count.**

**Flow duration.**

**Average packet size.**

**Minimum packet size.**

**Maximum packet size.**

**Packet-size variation.**

**Packet timing statistics.**

**Request frequency.**

**Directional packet counts.**



**The final feature set will be determined during the feature-engineering phase.**



**16.10 Packet Timing Analysis**



**Timing information can provide useful behavioral characteristics.**



**The system may calculate:**



**Inter-arrival times.**

**Average inter-arrival time.**

**Minimum inter-arrival time.**

**Maximum inter-arrival time.**

**Timing variance.**

**Burst characteristics.**



**These values may help distinguish different traffic behaviors.**



**16.11 Protocol Analysis**



**The processing pipeline will identify relevant protocol information.**



**Potential protocol categories include:**



**TCP.**

**UDP.**

**DNS.**

**HTTP.**

**HTTPS/TLS.**

**Other protocols observed within the controlled laboratory.**



**Protocol information will be treated as one input to the feature-engineering process rather than a standalone maliciousness decision.**



**16.12 Destination Analysis**



**The system may analyze destination-related characteristics within the controlled environment.**



**Potential information includes:**



**Destination address.**

**Destination port.**

**Domain information where available.**

**Request frequency.**

**Communication frequency.**

**Destination diversity.**



**The system will avoid making unsupported conclusions solely from destination information.**



**16.13 Domain and Entropy Features**



**Where suitable data is available, the pipeline may calculate statistical properties of domain names or controlled payloads.**



**Potential measurements include:**



**String length.**

**Character distribution.**

**Entropy.**

**Number of unique characters.**

**Subdomain characteristics.**



**These measurements may become ML features during the feature-engineering stage.**



**16.14 Encrypted Traffic**



**The system may analyze metadata from encrypted traffic without attempting to bypass encryption on arbitrary third-party systems.**



**For controlled experiments, the project may use project-owned infrastructure where TLS termination is available.**



**Potential metadata includes:**



**Packet sizes.**

**Timing.**

**Flow duration.**

**Packet counts.**

**Directionality.**

**TLS-related metadata available to the capture environment.**

**16.15 Feature Extraction Boundary**



**The packet-processing subsystem will produce structured features for the ML pipeline.**



**The boundary is:**



**Raw PCAP**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Packet Parser**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Flow Processor**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Statistical Analysis**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Feature Validation**

&#x20;  **↓**

**ML Pipeline**



**The ML system will receive validated structured data rather than arbitrary raw files.**



**16.16 Feature Validation**



**Before ML inference, extracted features will be validated.**



**Validation may check:**



**Required features exist.**

**Data types are correct.**

**Values are within expected ranges.**

**Missing values are handled.**

**Feature ordering is consistent.**

**Feature version matches the model.**



**Invalid feature records will be rejected or handled through an explicitly defined error path.**



**16.17 Feature Versioning**



**The feature set will be versioned.**



**Example:**



**Feature Set v1**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Training Model v1**



**Feature Set v2**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Training Model v2**



**A model will only be used with the preprocessing and feature configuration for which it was validated.**



**16.18 Processing Status**



**The traffic-processing pipeline will expose processing states to the application.**



**Example:**



**CAPTURED**

&#x20;  **↓**

**VALIDATING**

&#x20;  **↓**

**PARSING**

**Resource monitoring.**

**Section 17: Machine Learning \& Detection Architecture**



**This is the main intelligence layer of Extension AI Guard.**



**It will define how we go from:**



**processed traffic → features → ML models → risk score → detection → explanation**



**## 17. Machine Learning and Detection Architecture**



**The Machine Learning and Detection subsystem is responsible for analyzing validated network-traffic features and determining whether observed browser-extension behavior resembles the benign or suspicious patterns represented in the project's training and evaluation datasets.**



**The ML subsystem will operate as a controlled detection component within the larger Extension AI Guard architecture.**



**The ML system will support both research experimentation and real-time inference.**



**### 17.1 ML Detection Pipeline**



**The overall ML pipeline is:**



**```text**

**PCAP**

&#x20; **↓**

**Packet Processing**

&#x20; **↓**

**Flow Reconstruction**

&#x20; **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20; **↓**

**Feature Validation**

&#x20; **↓**

**Preprocessing**

&#x20; **↓**

**ML Model**

&#x20; **↓**

**Prediction**

&#x20; **↓**

**Risk Classification**

&#x20; **↓**

**Security Result**

**17.2 ML Objectives**



**The ML subsystem will aim to:**



**Identify behavioral differences between benign and suspicious traffic.**

**Generate consistent predictions from validated network features.**

**Provide measurable detection performance.**

**Support multiple model experiments.**

**Preserve model and dataset version information.**

**Provide evidence that can be displayed to analysts.**

**Support real-time inference after the model is validated.**

**17.3 Training Data**



**The initial training data will be generated from controlled laboratory experiments.**



**The dataset-generation process is:**



**Benign Extension**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Benign Traffic**

&#x20;      **↓**

**PCAP**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Processing**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Benign Features**



**and:**



**Suspicious Traffic Simulator**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Controlled Suspicious Traffic**

&#x20;      **↓**

**PCAP**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Processing**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Suspicious Features**



**The resulting feature records will be combined into a labeled dataset.**



**17.4 Dataset Labels**



**Each training example will have an appropriate label representing the controlled experiment category.**



**An initial conceptual labeling scheme is:**



**0 = Benign**

**1 = Suspicious**



**The final labeling strategy will be defined during dataset implementation.**



**Labels will represent the behavior category used to generate the controlled experiment and will not automatically imply that every real-world sample with similar characteristics is malicious.**



**17.5 Dataset Quality**



**Before training, datasets will be checked for:**



**Missing values.**

**Duplicate records.**

**Invalid values.**

**Incorrect labels.**

**Class imbalance.**

**Feature inconsistencies.**

**Data leakage.**

**Unexpected distributions.**



**Dataset quality checks will be documented and reproducible.**



**17.6 Train, Validation, and Test Data**



**The dataset will be divided into appropriate subsets.**



**A conceptual structure is:**



**Complete Dataset**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Training Set**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Validation Set**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Test Set**



**The final split strategy will be selected during implementation.**



**Care will be taken to prevent related traffic samples from causing unrealistic leakage between training and test data.**



**17.7 Feature Preprocessing**



**Before model training and inference, the feature data may require preprocessing.**



**Possible operations include:**



**Missing-value handling.**

**Scaling.**

**Normalization.**

**Encoding categorical information.**

**Feature selection.**

**Outlier handling where appropriate.**



**The preprocessing configuration will be versioned alongside the model.**



**17.8 Feature Selection**



**The initial feature candidates may include:**



**Packet count.**

**Byte count.**

**Flow duration.**

**Average packet size.**

**Packet-size variation.**

**Inter-arrival-time statistics.**

**Request frequency.**

**Directionality.**

**Protocol information.**

**Destination characteristics.**

**Domain-length information where available.**

**Entropy-related measurements.**



**The final feature set will be determined through experimentation and evaluation.**



**17.9 Baseline Model**



**A simple baseline model will be established before more advanced models are evaluated.**



**The baseline provides a reference point for determining whether later models produce meaningful improvement.**



**The baseline model and its results will be documented.**



**17.10 Random Forest Model**



**Random Forest will be evaluated as one of the primary classical ML models.**



**The model is suitable for experimentation with structured tabular features and can provide useful feature-importance information.**



**The project will record:**



**Model configuration.**

**Training dataset version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Evaluation results.**

**Model version.**

**17.11 XGBoost Model**



**XGBoost will be evaluated as another primary classical ML model.**



**It will be compared against the baseline and Random Forest model.**



**The evaluation will consider both predictive performance and practical inference requirements.**



**17.12 Model Comparison**



**The project will compare candidate models using consistent evaluation data.**



**Potential comparison metrics include:**



**Accuracy.**

**Precision.**

**Recall.**

**F1-score.**

**ROC-AUC.**

**Confusion matrix.**

**Inference performance.**



**The model with the strongest overall suitability will be selected based on the project's defined evaluation criteria rather than accuracy alone.**



**17.13 False Positives and False Negatives**



**The project will explicitly evaluate false positives and false negatives.**



**A false positive occurs when benign behavior is incorrectly classified as suspicious.**



**A false negative occurs when suspicious behavior is incorrectly classified as benign.**



**Both are important because a security detector that produces excessive false positives may become difficult for users to trust, while excessive false negatives may allow suspicious behavior to pass undetected.**



**17.14 Risk Classification**



**The detection system may convert model output into a user-friendly risk classification.**



**A conceptual representation is:**



**Model Prediction**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Confidence / Probability**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Risk Classification**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Low / Medium / High**



**The exact thresholds will be determined through validation rather than arbitrarily selected.**



**17.15 Detection Evidence**



**The system should provide supporting information for a detection where possible.**



**Potential evidence includes:**



**Relevant traffic statistics.**

**Important feature values.**

**Observed behavior patterns.**

**Model version.**

**Test profile.**

**Analysis timestamp.**



**The system will distinguish between evidence observed in the traffic and conclusions produced by the model.**



**17.16 Explainability**



**The ML subsystem will support explanations suitable for both beginners and experts.**



**For beginners:**



**The extension generated unusual network behavior**

**compared with the normal baseline.**



**For analysts:**



**The detection was influenced by observed traffic**

**features such as flow frequency, packet statistics,**

**timing characteristics, and other validated features.**



**Where appropriate, explainability techniques may be evaluated during implementation.**



**17.17 Beginner Detection Experience**



**The beginner user should not need to understand machine-learning terminology.**



**The system will translate the technical result into a simple explanation.**



**Example:**



**Detection Complete**



**Risk Level: HIGH**



**The tested extension showed network behavior**

**that differs significantly from the normal baseline.**



**Why this matters:**

**The system observed patterns that matched**

**the suspicious behavior used in the controlled test.**



**What you can do:**

**Review the extension's behavior and inspect**

**the detailed analysis.**



**The wording will be refined during frontend implementation.**



**17.18 Analyst Detection Experience**



**Analysts may access additional information such as:**



**Prediction probability.**

**Feature contribution information where supported.**

**Model version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Dataset version.**

**Confusion-matrix results.**

**Detection evidence.**

**Flow statistics.**



**This allows the analyst to investigate how the result was produced.**



**17.19 Research Detection Experience**



**Research users may access:**



**Training results.**

**Validation results.**

**Test results.**

**Model comparisons.**

**Feature experiments.**

**Hyperparameter experiments.**

**Classical ML results.**

**Quantum ML comparison results.**



**Research functionality will remain separated from ordinary beginner workflows.**



**17.20 Model Versioning**



**Every deployed or evaluated model will have a version identifier.**



**Example:**



**Random Forest**

**Version: RF-v1**



**XGBoost**

**Version: XGB-v1**



**The exact naming convention will be finalized during implementation.**



**Each model version will be associated with:**



**Dataset version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Preprocessing version.**

**Training configuration.**

**Evaluation results.**

**17.21 Model Serialization**



**Validated models will be serialized for reuse during inference.**



**The project may use:**



**Joblib.**

**ONNX.**



**The final serialization format will depend on model compatibility and deployment requirements.**



**Serialized model artifacts will be validated before being used by the inference engine.**



**17.22 Inference Architecture**



**The inference pipeline will be designed to operate independently from model-training workflows.**



**The conceptual architecture is:**



**Processed Traffic**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Preprocessing**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Serialized Model**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Inference**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Prediction**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Risk Classification**



**Training will not occur automatically during normal user detection.**



**17.23 Real-Time Detection**



**After the inference pipeline has been validated, the system may support real-time or near-real-time detection.**



**The conceptual flow is:**



**Live / Recent Traffic**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Flow Processing**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Inference**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Detection**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Dashboard**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Alerting**



**Real-time detection will be introduced only after the offline pipeline is stable.**



**17.24 ML Security**



**The ML subsystem will protect against incorrect or malformed inputs.**



**Controls will include:**



**Feature validation.**

**Model-version validation.**

**Preprocessing consistency.**

**Input-range checks.**

**Model artifact integrity checks where appropriate.**

**Controlled model deployment.**

**Dataset validation.**



**The ML system will not blindly trust client-supplied feature values.**



**17.25 Data Leakage Prevention**



**The project will take measures to prevent data leakage during model development.**



**For example:**



**Related traffic captures should not be unintentionally distributed across training and test sets.**

**Test information should not directly encode the target label through an artificial shortcut.**

**Evaluation data should remain independent from training decisions.**

**Preprocessing should be fitted using the appropriate training data.**

**17.26 Model Evaluation Requirements**



**Before a model is considered suitable for inference, it should pass defined evaluation requirements.**



**Evaluation will consider:**



**Predictive performance.**

**False-positive behavior.**

**False-negative behavior.**

**Generalization.**

**Inference speed.**

**Resource requirements.**

**Stability across controlled experiments.**

**17.27 Model Selection**



**The final production candidate will be selected through documented comparison.**



**The decision will consider:**



**Performance**

&#x20;   **+**

**Reliability**

&#x20;   **+**

**Interpretability**

&#x20;   **+**

**Inference Cost**

&#x20;   **+**

**Security**

&#x20;   **+**

**Maintainability**



**The highest raw accuracy will not automatically determine the final model.**



**17.28 ML-to-Backend Integration**



**The detection engine will communicate its result to the backend.**



**The flow is:**



**ML Inference**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Detection Result**

**Backend API**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Database**

&#x20;    **↓**

&#x20;    **↓**

**AI Security Assistant**

**The AI Security Assistant will explain validated detection results.**



**The assistant will receive structured detection information rather than unrestricted access to the ML system.**



**The flow is:**



**ML Detection**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Structured Result**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Backend**

&#x20;     **↓**

**AI Security Assistant**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Human-Friendly Explanation**



**The AI assistant will not override the authoritative detection result.**



**17.30 Classical and Quantum Comparison**



**The project will compare classical ML approaches with experimental Quantum ML approaches.**

**Accuracy.**

**Precision.**

**Recall.**

**F1-score.**

**ROC-AUC.**

**Training behavior.**

**Inference behavior.**

**Computational requirements.**

**17.31 ML Goal**



**The primary goal of the ML subsystem is to provide a measurable and reproducible detection layer that converts validated network-behavior features into useful security classifications.**



**The complete intelligence pipeline is:**



**Controlled Extension**

&#x20;       **↓**

**## 18. Quantum Machine Learning Research Architecture**



**The Quantum Machine Learning subsystem will provide an experimental research layer for Extension AI Guard.**



**Its purpose is to investigate whether quantum machine-learning approaches can be applied to the network-behavior classification problem and to compare their results against established classical machine-learning models.**



**Quantum ML will not be assumed to outperform classical ML.**



**The project will use measurable experimental results to determine the usefulness of the quantum approach.**



**### 18.1 Quantum ML Objective**



**The Quantum ML research objective is:**



**```text**

**Can a quantum-inspired or quantum-machine-learning**

**approach classify controlled network behavior**

**effectively when compared with classical ML models?**



**The experiment will therefore focus on a fair comparison between classical and quantum approaches using compatible datasets and evaluation procedures.**



**18.2 Quantum ML Position in the Architecture**



**The Quantum ML subsystem will operate alongside the classical ML research pipeline.**



**The architecture is:**



&#x20;                   **Feature Dataset**

&#x20;                         **↓**

&#x20;                **┌────────┴────────┐**

&#x20;                **↓                 ↓**

&#x20;         **Classical ML       Quantum ML**

&#x20;                **↓                 ↓**

&#x20;         **RF / XGBoost       VQC / QSVM**

&#x20;                **↓                 ↓**

&#x20;                **└────────┬────────┘**

&#x20;                         **↓**

&#x20;                  **Model Comparison**

&#x20;                         **↓**

&#x20;                 **Research Findings**

**18.3 Quantum ML Input**



**The Quantum ML subsystem will receive validated feature data produced by the same traffic-processing pipeline used by classical ML.**



**The input flow is:**



**Controlled Traffic**

&#x20;      **↓**

**PCAP**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Packet Processing**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Flow Processing**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Feature Engineering**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Feature Validation**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Quantum ML Dataset**



**This ensures that the quantum experiment is based on the same underlying network-behavior information.**



**18.4 Dataset Consistency**



**The quantum experiment will use appropriately prepared data derived from the project's controlled datasets.**



**The project will document:**



**Dataset version.**

**Feature-set version.**

**Preprocessing method.**

**Training split.**

**Evaluation split.**

**Experiment configuration.**



**The same evaluation principles used for classical models will be applied to the quantum experiment wherever technically practical.**



**18.5 Feature Reduction**



**Quantum circuits generally operate with a limited number of qubits.**



**Therefore, the complete network feature set may need to be reduced before quantum encoding.**



**Possible techniques include:**



**Feature selection.**

**Statistical filtering.**

**Dimensionality reduction.**

**Principal Component Analysis.**

**Domain-informed feature selection.**



**The final technique will be selected experimentally.**



**18.6 Quantum Feature Encoding**



**Selected classical features will be transformed into values suitable for quantum-circuit encoding.**



**A conceptual flow is:**



**Classical Features**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Scaling / Normalization**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Feature Reduction**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Quantum Encoding**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Quantum Circuit**



**The encoding method will be documented for each experiment.**



**18.7 Quantum Simulator**



**The initial Quantum ML implementation will use quantum simulators.**



**This allows the project to develop and evaluate quantum algorithms without requiring access to physical quantum hardware.**



**The simulator environment will provide a reproducible research platform.**



**Physical quantum hardware may be considered later if it provides meaningful research value and is available.**



**18.8 Quantum Frameworks**



**The planned quantum frameworks are:**



**Qiskit.**

**PennyLane where appropriate.**



**The project will select the framework that best supports the specific experiment.**



**The architecture will avoid introducing unnecessary quantum dependencies when they do not contribute to the research objective.**



**18.9 Variational Quantum Classifier**



**A Variational Quantum Classifier may be evaluated as one of the primary quantum approaches.**



**The conceptual pipeline is:**



**Input Features**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Quantum Encoding**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Parameterized Quantum Circuit**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Measurement**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Class Prediction**



**Circuit parameters will be optimized using an appropriate classical optimization process.**



**18.10 Quantum Support Vector Machine**



**A Quantum Support Vector Machine or quantum-kernel-based approach may also be investigated.**



**The conceptual architecture is:**



**Input Features**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Quantum Feature Map**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Quantum Kernel**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Classification**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Prediction**



**The final quantum algorithms will depend on compatibility with the selected dataset and available simulation resources.**



**18.11 Hybrid Quantum-Classical Architecture**



**The Quantum ML system will use a hybrid architecture where appropriate.**



**The general workflow is:**



**Classical Data**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Classical Preprocessing**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Quantum Circuit**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Quantum Measurement**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Classical Optimization**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Updated Parameters**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Quantum Circuit**



**This approach reflects the practical architecture of many current quantum-machine-learning experiments.**



**18.12 Quantum Experiment Lifecycle**



**Each quantum experiment will follow a controlled lifecycle:**



**Experiment Definition**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Dataset Selection**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Feature Selection**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Preprocessing**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Quantum Encoding**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Circuit Construction**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Training / Optimization**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Evaluation**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Comparison**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Research Result**

**18.13 Quantum Experiment Metadata**



**Each experiment will record appropriate metadata.**



**Potential information includes:**



**Experiment identifier.**

**18.14 Quantum Evaluation**



**Quantum models will be evaluated using appropriate metrics.**



**Potential metrics include:**



**Accuracy.**

**Precision.**

**Recall.**

**F1-score.**

**ROC-AUC where applicable.**

**Confusion matrix.**

**Training behavior.**

**Inference behavior.**

**Computational requirements.**



**The metrics will be interpreted according to the limitations of the dataset and experimental setup.**



**18.15 Classical Baseline**



**The classical ML results will act as the baseline for the quantum experiment.**



**The primary classical candidates are:**



**Random Forest**

**XGBoost**



**The quantum models will be compared against these results using compatible evaluation procedures.**



**18.16 Fair Comparison**



**The project will attempt to make the classical-versus-quantum comparison as fair as practical.**



**The comparison will document:**



**Dataset.**

**Features.**

**Data splits.**

**Preprocessing.**

**Evaluation metrics.**

**Training configuration.**

**Model configuration.**

**Hardware or simulator environment.**



**The project will clearly distinguish experimental limitations from measured improvements.**



**18.17 Quantum Advantage Claim**



**The project will not claim quantum advantage merely because a quantum model produces a result.**



**Any claim of improvement must be supported by experimental evidence.**



**The final report will distinguish between:**



**Observed Result**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Experimental Improvement**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Practical Benefit**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Quantum Advantage**



**These are not automatically equivalent.**

**Possible artifacts include:**

**18.23 Quantum Security Considerations**



**The Quantum ML environment will follow the project's general security principles.**



**Controls include:**



**Validated input data.**

**Controlled experiment execution.**

**Resource limits.**

**Versioned experiments.**

**No arbitrary circuit execution from untrusted users.**

**Restricted research functionality.**

**Secure handling of experiment artifacts.**

**18.24 Quantum Resource Management**



**Quantum simulation can require significant computational resources.**



**The project will consider:**



**Number of qubits.**

**Circuit depth.**

**Number of simulation shots.**

**Training iterations.**

**Dataset size.**

**CPU and memory requirements.**

**Experiment time.**



**Experiments will therefore be designed progressively rather than immediately using unnecessarily large circuits.**



**18.25 Production Relationship**

**The primary production detection path will use the validated classical ML model unless experimental evidence demonstrates that a quantum approach is practical and reliable for the deployment environment.**



**The architecture is:**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Research Conclusion**



**The final conclusion will clearly state what was demonstrated and what remains experimental.**



**18.27 Quantum ML Goal**



**The goal of the Quantum ML subsystem is to provide a technically meaningful and scientifically measurable investigation into quantum approaches for browser-extension network-behavior classification.**



**The final research pipeline is:**



**Controlled Network Traffic**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Validated Feature Dataset**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Feature Reduction**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Quantum Encoding**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Quantum Model**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Evaluation**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Classical Comparison**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Research Findings**



**Quantum ML therefore strengthens the research value of Extension AI Guard without making unsupported claims that quantum computing is automatically superior.**



**## 19. Real-Time Detection and Inference Architecture**



**The Real-Time Detection and Inference subsystem is responsible for converting newly observed network activity into security predictions as quickly and reliably as practical.**



**This subsystem connects the traffic-processing layer, trained ML model, backend API, dashboard, AI Security Assistant, and alerting system.**



**The real-time pipeline will only use validated components that have already passed offline testing.**



**### 19.1 Real-Time Detection Objective**



**The objective is to allow Extension AI Guard to analyze controlled browser-extension traffic and produce a security result without requiring the user to manually process PCAP files.**



**The conceptual workflow is:**



**```text**

**User Starts Test**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Extension Generates Traffic**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Traffic Capture**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Flow Processing**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Feature Validation**

&#x20;      **↓**

**ML Inference**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Risk Assessment**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Backend**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Dashboard**

&#x20;      **↓**

**AI Explanation / Alert**

**19.2 Real-Time Detection Architecture**



**The main architecture is:**



&#x20;                **Browser Extension**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;                **Network Activity**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;                **Capture Engine**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;                **Traffic Processor**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;                **Feature Extractor**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;                **Feature Validator**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;               **Inference Service**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;             **┌─────────┴─────────┐**

&#x20;             **↓                   ↓**

&#x20;       **Detection Result      Risk Score**

&#x20;             **↓                   ↓**

&#x20;             **└─────────┬─────────┘**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;                  **Backend API**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;             **┌─────────┼─────────┐**

&#x20;             **↓         ↓         ↓**

&#x20;        **Database   Dashboard   Alerting**

&#x20;                       **↓**

&#x20;               **AI Security Assistant**

**19.3 Detection Modes**



**Extension AI Guard will support different detection modes.**



**The initial conceptual modes are:**



**1. Guided Test Mode**

**2. Manual Analysis Mode**

**3. Real-Time Detection Mode**

**4. Research Mode**



**Each mode will expose only the functionality appropriate to the user.**



**19.4 Guided Test Mode**



**Guided Test Mode is designed for first-time users.**



**The user experience is:**



**Open Extension AI Guard**

&#x20;       **↓**

**AI Assistant Welcomes User**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Choose "Start Guided Test"**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Select Test Type**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Environment Check**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Start Controlled Test**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Traffic Analysis**

&#x20;       **↓**

**ML Detection**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Security Result**

&#x20;       **↓**

**AI Explanation**



**The user should not need to manually configure TShark, PCAP processing, ML preprocessing, or model loading.**



**19.5 Manual Analysis Mode**



**Manual Analysis Mode is designed for users who want greater control.**



**The user may select an existing supported analysis artifact and request processing through the application.**



**The workflow is:**



**Select Analysis Input**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Validation**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Packet Processing**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Feature Extraction**

&#x20;      **↓**

**ML Inference**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Result**



**Only supported and validated inputs will be accepted.**



**19.6 Real-Time Detection Mode**



**Real-Time Detection Mode continuously or periodically evaluates newly available traffic information during an active controlled test.**



**The conceptual flow is:**



**Traffic Appears**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Capture**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Flow Update**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Feature Update**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Inference**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Risk Update**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Dashboard Update**



**The exact processing interval will be determined during implementation and performance testing.**



**19.7 Inference Service**



**The Inference Service will be responsible for loading the validated ML model and generating predictions.**



**Its responsibilities include:**



**Loading the approved model.**

**Loading the matching preprocessing configuration.**

**Validating feature input.**

**Performing preprocessing.**

**Running inference.**

**Producing prediction output.**

**Returning model metadata.**



**The service will not train models during normal detection.**



**19.8 Model Loading**



**The inference service will load only approved model artifacts.**



**The model-loading process is:**



**Model Artifact**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Integrity / Compatibility Check**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Model Version Check**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Feature Version Check**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Preprocessing Version Check**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Load Model**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Ready for Inference**



**If compatibility checks fail, the model will not be used.**



**19.9 Inference Request**



**A conceptual inference request may contain:**



**Test ID**

**Feature Set Version**

**Feature Values**

**Processing Timestamp**



**The exact API schema will be defined later during backend implementation.**



**Client applications will not be trusted to provide authoritative model metadata.**



**19.10 Inference Response**



**A conceptual inference response may contain:**



**Prediction**

**Risk Level**

**Confidence / Probability**

**Model Version**

**Feature Version**

**Detection Timestamp**

**Detection Identifier**



**Additional evidence may be attached where supported.**



**19.11 Prediction Lifecycle**



**Each prediction will follow a controlled lifecycle:**



**Feature Data Received**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Input Validation**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Preprocessing**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Model Inference**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Prediction Validation**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Risk Classification**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Evidence Generation**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Result Persistence**

&#x20;       **↓**

**Dashboard / Alert Update**

**19.12 Risk Classification**



**The model output will be translated into an understandable risk classification.**



**The conceptual structure is:**



**Model Output**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Validated Probability / Score**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Risk Threshold Logic**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Low / Medium / High**



**Thresholds will be determined through model evaluation and documented configuration.**



**They will not be selected only for visual presentation.**



**19.13 Confidence Handling**



**The system may display model confidence or probability where the selected model supports a meaningful interpretation.**



**The interface will clearly distinguish between:**



**Prediction**

**Confidence / Probability**

**Risk Classification**



**These values are related but are not necessarily identical.**



**19.14 Evidence Generation**



**Each detection should contain enough structured information to explain why the system produced the result.**



**Possible evidence includes:**



**Flow statistics.**

**Packet statistics.**

**Timing characteristics.**

**Communication frequency.**

**Relevant feature values.**

**Model version.**

**Test profile.**

**Detection timestamp.**



**Evidence will be generated from validated processing results.**



**19.15 Detection Record**



**A detection record will conceptually contain:**



**Detection ID**

**Test ID**

**User / Owner Reference**

**Timestamp**

**Prediction**

**Risk Level**

**Confidence / Probability**

**Model Version**

**Feature Version**

**Evidence Reference**

**Status**



**The final database schema will be defined separately.**



**19.16 Real-Time Database Flow**



**The backend will persist important detection events.**



**The flow is:**



**Inference Service**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Detection Result**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Backend API**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Validation**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Database**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Dashboard**



**The database will provide historical detection information while the frontend will provide the live user experience.**



**19.17 Dashboard Updates**



**The dashboard may receive detection updates through an appropriate real-time mechanism.**



**The conceptual architecture is:**



**Detection Engine**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Backend**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Real-Time Event**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Frontend**

&#x20;      **↓**

**Dashboard Update**



**The final communication mechanism will be selected during backend implementation.**



**19.18 Live Risk State**



**During an active test, the dashboard may maintain a current risk state.**



**Example:**



**Test Started**

&#x20;    **↓**

**No Detection**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Low Risk**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Suspicious Pattern Detected**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Medium Risk**

&#x20;    **↓**

**Additional Evidence**

&#x20;    **↓**

**High Risk**



**Risk updates must be based on actual validated detections.**



**The system must not artificially escalate risk merely because time has passed.**



**19.19 Detection Deduplication**



**Repeated observations of the same behavior may produce multiple model predictions.**



**The backend will therefore support a strategy for grouping or deduplicating related detection events where appropriate.**



**The goal is to avoid overwhelming the user with duplicate alerts.**



**19.20 Detection State Management**



**Detection records may use states such as:**



**OBSERVED**

**ANALYZING**

**DETECTED**

**REVIEWED**

**RESOLVED**



**The final state model will be defined during backend implementation.**



**19.21 Alert Decision**



**The alerting subsystem will consume validated detection events.**



**The conceptual flow is:**



**Detection**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Risk Evaluation**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Alert Policy**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Should Alert?**

&#x20;  **/      \\**

&#x20;**YES       NO**

&#x20;**↓         ↓**

**Alert     Store**



**Alert rules will be configurable and documented.**



**19.22 AI Security Assistant Integration**



**The AI Security Assistant will receive structured detection information through the backend.**



**The flow is:**



**ML Detection**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Structured Security Result**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Backend API**

&#x20;     **↓**

**AI Security Assistant**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Human-Friendly Explanation**



**The assistant will explain the result but will not modify the underlying ML prediction.**



**19.23 First-Time User Experience**



**The first-time user journey will be intentionally simple.**



**The user will see:**



**Welcome**

&#x20;  **↓**

**AI Assistant Introduction**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Explain What Extension AI Guard Does**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Check Environment**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Choose a Safe Test**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Run Test**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Observe Analysis**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Receive Result**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Understand Why**



**The AI Assistant will guide the user through each stage.**



**19.24 AI Assistant Boundaries**



**The AI Assistant will operate as a guidance and explanation layer.**



**It may:**



**Explain security concepts.**

**Explain detection results.**

**Guide users through tests.**

**Explain dashboard information.**

**Recommend safe next steps.**



**It will not:**



**Override ML predictions.**

**Execute arbitrary commands.**

**Modify security controls without authorization.**

**Access unrestricted system resources.**

**Automatically execute untrusted files.**

**19.25 Real-Time Error Handling**



**The system will handle failures such as:**



**Capture failure.**

**Processing failure.**

**Feature validation failure.**

**Model loading failure.**

**Inference failure.**

**Backend communication failure.**

**Database failure.**

**Dashboard connection failure.**



**The system should report an understandable status to the user while retaining appropriate technical information for debugging.**

**When possible, the pipeline will recover safely from temporary failures.**



**Example:**



**Temporary Processing Failure**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Retry / Recovery Logic**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Successful Processing**

&#x20;         **↓**

**Continue Detection**



**Repeated failures will terminate the affected test safely rather than continuously consuming resources.**



**19.27 Real-Time Resource Management**



**Real-time processing will be subject to resource controls.**



**The system will monitor or limit:**



**CPU usage.**

**Memory usage.**

**Capture size.**

**Processing duration.**

**Number of simultaneous tests.**

**Temporary storage.**



**These controls will help prevent resource exhaustion.**

**User**

&#x20;**↓**

&#x20;**↓**

**Authorization**

&#x20;**↓**

**Detection Operation**

**The real-time subsystem will follow the project's security architecture.**



**Important controls include:**



**Authentication.**

**Authorization.**

**Input validation.**

**Secure API communication.**

**Model validation.**

**Feature validation.**

**Rate limiting where appropriate.**

**Resource limits.**

**Audit logging.**

**Controlled test execution.**

**Secure error handling.**

**The promotion path is:**



**Training**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

**## 20. Backend API and Supabase Integration Architecture**



**The Backend API and Supabase Integration subsystem provides the central application layer connecting the frontend, authentication system, database, ML inference engine, traffic-analysis pipeline, AI Security Assistant, and alerting system.**



**The backend will use FastAPI to provide controlled REST APIs while Supabase/PostgreSQL will provide persistent application data storage.**



**The backend will act as the security boundary between users and internal project services.**



**### 20.1 Backend Architecture**



**The high-level backend architecture is:**



**```text**

**React Frontend**

&#x20;     **↓**

**FastAPI Backend**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Authentication / Authorization**

&#x20;     **↓**

**API Validation**

&#x20;     **↓**

**Application Services**

&#x20;     **↓**

**┌─────┼──────────┬───────────┐**

**↓     ↓          ↓           ↓**

**DB    ML       Traffic      Alerts**

**↓     ↓          ↓           ↓**

**Supabase  Inference   Processing   n8n**

**20.2 Backend Responsibilities**



**The backend will be responsible for:**



**User authentication integration.**

**Authorization.**

**Role management.**

**API request validation.**

**Test-session management.**

**Detection management.**

**Traffic-analysis coordination.**

**ML inference coordination.**

**Database operations.**

**Audit logging.**

**Dashboard data delivery.**

**Alert coordination.**

**Security-policy enforcement.**

**20.3 Frontend-to-Backend Flow**



**The frontend will communicate with the backend through HTTPS APIs.**



**The basic flow is:**



**User**

&#x20;**↓**

**React Frontend**

&#x20;**↓**

**HTTPS Request**

&#x20;**↓**

**FastAPI**

&#x20;**↓**

**Authentication**

&#x20;**↓**

**Authorization**

&#x20;**↓**

**Validation**

&#x20;**↓**

**Application Logic**

&#x20;**↓**

**Response**

&#x20;**↓**

**React Frontend**



**The frontend will not directly access protected internal services.**



**20.4 API Layer**



**FastAPI will provide the application's REST API layer.**



**The API will be organized into logical groups rather than placing all functionality into a single large endpoint module.**



**Conceptual groups include:**



**/api/auth**

**/api/users**

**/api/tests**

**/api/extensions**

**/api/traffic**

**/api/detections**

**/api/models**

**User Login**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Authentication Provider**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Identity Token**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Frontend**

&#x20;   **↓**

**FastAPI**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Token Validation**

&#x20;   **↓**

**Required claims.**

**User identity.**

**Authorization context.**

**Authentication answers:**



**Who are you?**

**What are you allowed to do?**

**The conceptual flow is:**



**Request**

&#x20;**↓**

**Authentication**

&#x20;**↓**

**User Identity**

&#x20;**↓**

**Role / Permission Check**

&#x20;**↓**

&#x20;**├── YES → Continue**

**20.32 Row-Level Access**



**Where appropriate, database-level access controls such as Row Level Security may be used.**



**The purpose is to ensure that users cannot access records belonging to other users simply by changing an identifier in an API request.**



**The authorization design will be implemented consistently between the API and database layers.**



**20.33 User-Owned Resources**



**Resources created by a user should be associated with an appropriate owner or authorization context.**



**The conceptual relationship is:**



**User**

&#x20;**↓**

**Test**

&#x20;**↓**

**Traffic Capture**

&#x20;**↓**

**Detection**

&#x20;**↓**

**Evidence**



**The backend will verify ownership or appropriate role permissions before returning protected resources.**



**20.34 Database Transactions**



**Operations involving multiple related database records will use appropriate transaction handling where required.**



**For example:**



**Create Test**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Create Processing Record**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Start Analysis**



**The system should avoid leaving inconsistent records when an intermediate operation fails.**



**20.35 Database Integrity**



**The database design will use appropriate:**



**Primary keys.**

**Foreign keys.**

**Unique constraints.**

**Not-null constraints.**

**Check constraints.**

**Indexes.**



**These controls will reduce inconsistent application data.**



**20.36 Database Indexing**



**Indexes will be introduced for frequently queried fields.**

**User ID.**

**Test ID.**

**Detection ID.**

**Timestamp.**

**Risk level.**

**Status.**

**Potential protected operations include:**



**Authentication-related requests.**

**Test creation.**

**Analysis requests.**

**Research experiments.**

**Alert operations.**



**Rate limits will be designed according to the deployment environment.**



**20.38 CORS Security**



**The backend will use a controlled CORS configuration.**



**Only approved frontend origins will be permitted in production.**



**Wildcard origins will not be used for sensitive production configurations unless explicitly justified.**



**20.39 HTTPS**



**Production API communication will use HTTPS.**



**The architecture is:**



**Browser**

&#x20;  **↓**

**HTTPS**

&#x20;  **↓**

**FastAPI**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Internal Services**

&#x20;  **↓**

**Supabase**



**Sensitive information should not be transmitted through unencrypted production HTTP connections.**



**20.40 Secret Management**



**The system will protect:**



**Database credentials.**

**Authentication secrets.**

**API keys.**

**AI service credentials.**

**Telegram credentials.**

**n8n credentials.**



**Secrets will not be placed directly inside source code.**



**20.41 Backend Logging**

**Errors.**

**Detection events.**

**Backend**

**Database**

**ML Service**

**Traffic Processor**

**20.43 Service Availability**



**The backend should distinguish between:**



**Healthy**

**Degraded**

**Unavailable**



**For example, the API may remain available even if a research-only Quantum ML service is temporarily unavailable.**



**20.44 Background Processing**



**Long-running operations should not block normal API requests.**



**Examples include:**



**PCAP processing.**

**Large dataset processing.**

**ML experiments.**

**Quantum simulation.**

**Report generation.**



**These operations may use background workers or task queues when required.**



**20.45 Job Status**

**The conceptual lifecycle is:**



**QUEUED**

&#x20; **↓**

**RUNNING**

&#x20; **↓**

**COMPLETED**



**or:**



**QUEUED**

&#x20; **↓**

**RUNNING**

&#x20; **↓**

**FAILED**

**20.47 AI Assistant Security Boundary**



**The AI assistant will be treated as an untrusted reasoning layer from a security perspective.**



**It must not automatically:**



**Execute operating-system commands.**

**Modify database records without authorization.**

**Change model configuration.**

**Disable security controls.**

**Access arbitrary files.**

**Execute arbitrary network requests.**



**Any privileged action must pass through authorized application services.**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;  **↓**

&#x20;     **↓**

&#x20;     **↓**

&#x20;    **↓**

&#x20;    **↓**

&#x20;    **↓**

**20.53 API Security Testing**

**Input validation.**

**Rate limiting.**

**CORS configuration.**

**Injection risks.**

**Sensitive data exposure.**

**Improper error handling.**



**Testing will be performed within the project's controlled environment.**



**20.54 OWASP Alignment**

**Injection.**

**Security logging and monitoring.**

**Server-side request risks.**

**Security misconfiguration.**
